distributionSigningAttemptedAndWhyItFail.attempt: Re-archive with CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual, CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY='Apple Distribution', PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER='iOS Team Store Provisioning Profile: com.nsantulli.econbyte' — the command recorded in the previous packet revision.
distributionSigningAttemptedAndWhyItFail.result: ARCHIVE FAILED with two errors: the profile 'doesn't include signing certificate Apple Distribution: NICHOLAS PATRICK SANTULLI (Q2DM9FSRL4)', and the profile 'is Xcode managed, but signing settings require a manually managed profile'.
distributionSigningAttemptedAndWhyItFail.rootCause: The locally installed App Store profile (expires 2027-06-01, Xcode-managed) embeds a distribution certificate with SHA1 B2CF464AAC0E013CA373CEDB2DA4299DB4438549. The distribution identity actually in the keychain is SHA1 4161108AB0A51FA62347816ED01B33A3EFDA3F81. The profile was issued against a SUPERSEDED distribution certificate, so no local combination of the two can sign for distribution.
distributionSigningAttemptedAndWhyItFail.consequence: Distribution signing cannot be produced on this host without an authenticated Apple Developer session to regenerate the profile against the current certificate. Task 6a is barred from provisioning updates, which mutate the developer account.
distributionSigningAttemptedAndWhyItFail.ownerAction6b: In an authenticated Xcode session, let Xcode refresh the App Store provisioning profile for com.nsantulli.econbyte against the current Apple Distribution certificate, then either export this archive with distribution signing (xcodebuild -exportArchive with an app-store-connect export options plist) or re-archive with manual distribution signing. The archived binary does not change in either case; only the signature does.
distributionSigningAttemptedAndWhyItFail.note: A development-signed archive is the normal Xcode intermediate: distribution signing is applied at export. The blocker here is the stale profile, not the archive.

d2Decision.status: CLOSED — ruled Option B on 2026-08-30 and applied in commit c911b161.
d2Decision.gate: Spec section 9.1 / CONTENT-DECISIONS.md D2 permitted the change only after the archive privacy report confirmed that the configured SDK path does not access tracking permission or IDFA.
d2Decision.reportOutcomeAgainstTheLiteralGate: NOT CONFIRMED. The GoogleMobileAds SDK is statically linked into the app executable (its embedded framework binary is a 51 KB stub), that code links AdSupport and carries the ATT status and advertisingIdentifier APIs, and Google's bundled manifest declares DeviceID with tracking = true. First-party code has no ATT or IDFA reference and never prompts.
d2Decision.rulingAuthority: Owner's standing blanket approval, exercised 2026-08-30, together with a controller precedent check. Task 6a did not take this decision unilaterally: it archived, reported, and escalated with both options costed, and applied Option B only after the ruling.

ownerItems.source: discovered in Task 6a while attempting the distribution re-archive
ownerItems.status: NEW — blocks upload, not the build
ownerItems.detail: The local App Store provisioning profile for com.nsantulli.econbyte embeds a superseded distribution certificate (profile cert SHA1 B2CF464A..., keychain identity SHA1 4161108A...). Distribution signing therefore cannot be produced on this host. An authenticated Xcode session must refresh the profile before export or upload.

sixBHandoff.name: Create a new distribution provisioning profile — the existing one cannot be refreshed
sixBHandoff.why: The profile on the build host (iOS Team Store Provisioning Profile: com.nsantulli.econbyte, expires 2027-06-01) is XCODE-MANAGED and embeds a superseded distribution certificate (profile cert SHA1 B2CF464AAC0E013CA373CEDB2DA4299DB4438549; the keychain identity is SHA1 4161108AB0A51FA62347816ED01B33A3EFDA3F81). The App Store Connect API cannot modify or regenerate an Xcode-managed profile, so there is nothing to 'refresh' — a new, manually-managed profile must be created.

primaryPath.call: POST /v1/profiles using the existing ASC API key
primaryPath.body: type: profiles; attributes { name: 'EconByte App Store 1.1', profileType: 'IOS_APP_STORE' }; relationships { bundleId: the bundleIds id for com.nsantulli.econbyte (GET /v1/bundleIds?filter[identifier]=com.nsantulli.econbyte), certificates: the certificates id whose serial/fingerprint matches the keychain Apple Distribution identity SHA1 4161108A... (GET /v1/certificates?filter[certificateType]=DISTRIBUTION) }
primaryPath.then: Download the returned profileContent (base64 .mobileprovision), install it on the build host, and use its name in AppStore/1.1/exportOptions.plist. The name in that file is already set to 'EconByte App Store 1.1' — keep them identical.
primaryPath.verify: GET /v1/profiles/{id}?include=certificates and confirm the linked certificate is the current distribution certificate, not B2CF464A...

sixBHandoff.fallbackPath: Owner-led authenticated Xcode session: open the project, enable automatic signing with team Q2DM9FSRL4, and let Xcode issue the profile. If this path is taken, switch exportOptions.plist signingStyle to 'automatic' and drop the provisioningProfiles dictionary.
sixBHandoff.note: Creating a profile mutates the developer account, which is why Task 6a did not do it.

sixBHandoff.name: Export the retained archive with distribution signing
sixBHandoff.exportOptions: AppStore/1.1/exportOptions.plist — committed. method app-store-connect, teamID Q2DM9FSRL4, signingStyle manual, signingCertificate 'Apple Distribution', provisioningProfiles maps com.nsantulli.econbyte to the step-1 profile, destination export, manageAppVersionAndBuildNumber false, uploadSymbols true.
sixBHandoff.verifyBeforeUpload: codesign -d --entitlements :- on the exported app must show get-task-allow ABSENT (or false). If it is still true, the export did not re-sign and the upload will be rejected.
sixBHandoff.note: The binary is unchanged by export; only the signature is. The archive hash in this packet remains the provenance record.

sixBHandoff.name: Upload build 6
sixBHandoff.mechanism: xcrun altool --upload-app, authenticated with the ASC API key by ID only
sixBHandoff.keyHandling: The .p8 stays at ~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/AuthKey_<ASC_KEY_ID>.p8 (or the path in the private_keys search path). Reference the key by ID and issuer ID on the command line. Never paste key material into a file, a log, or this repository.
sixBHandoff.alternative: xcodebuild -exportArchive with destination 'upload' in the export options plus -authenticationKeyPath <path to .p8> -authenticationKeyID <ASC_KEY_ID> -authenticationKeyIssuerID <ASC_ISSUER_ID>, which exports and uploads in one step. Use it only if you do not want to inspect the .ipa first; step 2's entitlement check is worth keeping.
sixBHandoff.afterUpload: Wait for processing to finish before the build can be selected — an accepted upload is not a processed build.
sixBHandoff.notarytoolNote: notarytool is for macOS notarization and does not apply to an iOS App Store submission. altool --upload-app is the correct tool here.

sixBHandoff.name: Attach, answer, submit
actions: Select build 6 on the 1.1 version record.
Attach both approved IAPs: com.nsantulli.econbyte.unlockall and com.nsantulli.econbyte.removeads.
Enter the App Privacy answers from privacyReport.d2Decision.ascAnswersBinding (identical to metadata.json appPrivacy.oneOneFinalAnswers). Do not carry over the 1.0 answers.
Enter the listing fields from AppStore/1.1/metadata.json and upload the six recommended screenshots.
Answer the age-rating questionnaire that ASC presents today rather than transferring the 1.0 answers.
Set phased release ON and manual release, then submit.
sixBHandoff.blockedUntil: The AdMob app ID, interstitial unit ID, console frequency caps and app-ads.txt are confirmed against the console (CONTENT-DECISIONS.md D6). This is still an Owner item and it blocks submission, not upload.

sixBHandoff.name: READBACK — re-read every mutation and record it
sixBHandoff.why: Portfolio lesson, recorded: 'visible:true is not live'. A successful write response proves the request was accepted, not that the store state is what you intended. Nothing in this release is considered done on the strength of a mutation response.
readAfterSubmitting: GET /v1/apps/6780714383/appStoreVersions?filter[versionString]=1.1 — record the version id and appStoreState.
GET /v1/appStoreVersions/{id}/build — record the build NUMBER returned and confirm it is 6, not merely that a build is attached.

GET /v1/appStoreVersions/{id}/relationships/appStoreVersionExperiments is not the check; for the purchases use GET /v1/appStoreVersions/{id}/appStoreVersionSubmission and the version's in-app-purchase relationship — record BOTH product identifiers as returned, com.nsantulli.econbyte.unlockall and com.nsantulli.econbyte.removeads.
GET /v1/apps/6780714383/appDataUsages (with its categories/purposes includes) — record the Device ID and Advertising Data entries and confirm the tracking flags read NO, matching ascAnswersBinding.
GET the version's app screenshots and confirm the uploaded set count and display type.
sixBHandoff.recordWhere: Append the readback results to this packet as a new 'sixBReadback' object with the timestamp, each endpoint, and the exact value returned. A readback that disagrees with the intent is a stop condition, not a note.
sixBHandoff.doNotClaim: Do not report 1.1 as submitted, or the privacy answers as entered, from a 2xx response alone.

sixBHandoff.name: After approval
actions: Verify public availability, both IAPs, and the privacy/support URLs on the live listing.
Create the three custom product pages in AppStore/1.1/custom-product-pages.json, each with only its own screenshot subset.
Begin the 24h/7d/30d metric collection in design section 15.2.

sixBReadback.$comment: Task 6b execution record. Every value below is a READ-BACK from App Store Connect after the corresponding write, not a restatement of a 2xx response. Written 2026-08-30. Credentials, key material and JWTs never appear here: the ASC API key is referenced by key ID only, and the issuer ID is redacted from every retained log.
sixBReadback.outcome: STOPPED BEFORE SUBMISSION — steps 1-3 complete, step 4 complete except App Privacy, step 5 readback performed, submission NOT made.

stopCondition.rule: Instruction stop condition: "any privacy-answer field the API won't accept as specified"; and step 5 makes the appDataUsages tracking readback mandatory.
stopCondition.finding: The App Privacy (data-usage) resources do not exist in the App Store Connect API as reachable by this key. Every documented and adjacent path returns HTTP 404 PATH_ERROR — not 403, not an empty collection. The 1.1 privacy answers in appPrivacy.oneOneFinalAnswers therefore cannot be entered through the API, and the mandatory step-5 readback confirming the tracking flags read NO cannot be performed at all.

probes.detail: The path provided does not match a defined resource type.
The app resource exposes 40 relationships; none of them is appDataUsages or any privacy-details equivalent. The absence is structural, not a permission failure.

stopCondition.whySubmittingAnywayWasRefused: The App Privacy answers currently on the app record are the superseded 1.0 answers, whose tracking flags are YES for Device ID and Advertising Data (appPrivacy.oneZeroAnswers). The shipped build-6 binary declares NSPrivacyTracking = false with DeviceID tracking = false, and metadata.json states in terms that the 1.0 answers must NEVER be entered for 1.1. Submitting now would submit version 1.1 under a privacy declaration that contradicts its own binary. That is a materially false declaration to Apple, not a formality, so the Owner's submit-asap directive was not read as authorising it. Everything that does not depend on the privacy answers has been completed and verified, so the remaining Owner action is a single screen.
stopCondition.ownerActionToClear: In App Store Connect (web UI, signed in as the Owner): App Privacy -> Edit. For "Device ID" and "Usage Data > Advertising Data", keep them COLLECTED with purpose Third-Party Advertising and Not Linked to User, and set USED FOR TRACKING = NO on both. Leave every other data type Not Collected. Publish the changes, then submit version 1.1 for review with phased release ON and manual release (both are already set on the version record — see releaseControls below). The exact answer set is appPrivacy.oneOneFinalAnswers in AppStore/1.1/metadata.json, identical to privacyReport.d2Decision.ascAnswersBinding.
stopCondition.notAttempted: The ASC web UI was not driven and no Apple ID credentials were handled. This step needs an authenticated Owner session.

inAppPurchases.reviewerNoteAddressed: The handoff's step-5 IAP endpoint was imprecise, as flagged. The corrected finding is recorded here with the exact endpoints and responses.

endpointsTried.note: This is the legacy path the handoff implied. It no longer exists on appStoreVersions.

The appStoreVersionSubmissions resource named in the handoff is the deprecated submission mechanism and holds nothing for this version. The current mechanism is /v1/reviewSubmissions with reviewSubmissionItems.
The version resource exposes 13 relationships; none is inAppPurchases.

authoritativeReadback.interpretation: Both product identifiers are present and read APPROVED — exactly the two the packet requires and the two pinned by GrowthSystemsTests.testBothApprovedProductIdentifiersArePreservedExactly. Because they are APPROVED they must NOT be added as reviewSubmissionItems: that item type is for purchases awaiting review, and an APPROVED product would be rejected. No action was required or possible, and none was taken.

phasedRelease.interpretation: Phased release is ON. INACTIVE is the correct pre-release state: the resource exists on the version, so the phased rollout is armed, and it moves to ACTIVE only once the Owner releases the approved build. The absence of this resource — not the INACTIVE value — is what would mean phased release is off.

openItems.status: STILL UNCONFIRMED. Carried forward, not cleared.
openItems.controllerRuling: The packet marks D6 submission-blocking (ownerItems.admob-ids-unconfirmed.blocksSubmission = true, sixBHandoff step 4 blockedUntil). The controller ruled that the Owner's explicit submit-asap directive OVERRIDES that agent-authored gate, so 6b proceeded through preparation without it. The override changes when D6 is checked, not whether it must be.
openItems.whatIsUnconfirmed: The Release AdMob app ID and interstitial unit ID reused from 1.0 are format-valid but have never been checked against the AdMob console. Also unconfirmed: that the console frequency caps are at least as conservative as the in-app caps (1 per foreground session, 2 per calendar day, 15 minutes apart, 2 completed sets apart), and that a current app-ads.txt is published.
openItems.risk: If the IDs are wrong, ads silently fail to fill and 1.1 ships with dead ad inventory — a revenue defect, not a review rejection. Wrong or absent console caps would let the served frequency exceed what the listing, the review notes and the 4+ rating were argued on.
openItems.whoCanClear: Owner only — it needs AdMob console access, which no agent has.
openItems.whenToClear: Before the Owner releases the approved build, and in any case as the first post-approval check in step 6.

openItems.detail: metadata.json app.name is "EconByte: Daily Economics" (25 chars) but the live App Store name is "EconByte". The name was NOT changed. It is a storefront identity change, it was not in the 6b metadata instruction (which enumerated what's-new, description, keywords, promo, subtitle), and nothing in the packet records it as an intended 1.1 change. Raised for the Owner rather than applied silently.

metadata.json listing.subtitle.changeFrom1_0 says "unchanged". It is not: the live subtitle read "Learn Economics. In 5 Minutes." and metadata.json specifies "Learn Inflation. In 5 Minutes.". The metadata.json value was applied as instructed, so 1.1 does change the subtitle. The annotation, not the value, was wrong.

metadata.json listing.urls.privacy is "https://dudleyapps.com/privacy/" (trailing slash); the appInfoLocalization holds "https://dudleyapps.com/privacy" (no slash). Both resolve to the canonical privacy page. Left as-is: the privacy URL was not in the 6b metadata instruction and the difference is cosmetic.
